name: Jehoahaz
overview: Jehoahaz was a male king of Israel, identified as the son of Jehu according to 2 Kings 10:35. The biblical record does not specify his tribal affiliation or additional notes beyond his royal status. His reign is noted within the historical context of Israel's monarchy.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehoahaz means 'y-h-v-h holds,' reflecting a theophoric element referencing the LORD. He is also referred to as Joahaz, meaning 'y-h-v-h grips, holds,' in 2 Kings 14:1. Both names emphasize God's sustaining power, though neither name is explicitly stated to be given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jehoahaz as the son of Jehu (2 Kings 10:35). Additionally, it is inferred that Joash was his father (2 Kings 13:9), though this is not directly stated. Beyond these relationships, the biblical text does not provide further family details.
scriptureSignificance: Jehoahaz is significant as a continuation of Jehu's dynastic line, serving as king of Israel during a turbulent period. His position as Jehu's son underscores the fulfillment of God's judgment on Israel's house through Jehu's anointed kingship. This lineage highlights the ongoing narrative of God's sovereignty and covenant faithfulness amidst Israel's history.
